_comment: What an agent may assume is installed. The task contract is language-neutral -- trace.json
is method_id plus outputs, and the instruction names no language -- so this file says what
the environment can actually run. It is published with the dataset because the agent
container is no-network: a tool that is missing here cannot be installed at run time, so a
gap is a benchmark defect rather than an agent failure, and it should be reported as one.
Field names in outputs are matched case-, underscore-, hyphen- and dot-insensitively, so
R's p.value, Python's p_value and Julia's pvalue all bind to the canonical pValue.

r.note: base stats plus skewness/kurtosis (e1071), Anderson-Darling (nortest), JSON output (jsonlite)

absent.octave: Debian bookworm ships no octave-cli; the full package pulls the Qt/GL stack
absent.julia: not packaged for Debian; a tarball plus a precompiled depot costs more than R and the JVM together
absent.network: the agent container runs no-network by design; nothing can be installed at run time

_comment: Where toolchains take different defensible defaults, the STAGE PAYLOAD declares which one
the stored truth used, and following the declaration is part of the task. Declarations
seen in this corpus: alternativeHypothesis, assumeEqualVariances, continuityCorrection,
confidenceLevel. Absent a declaration, use the two-sided, no-continuity-correction,
